pages.text: Nora, an ancient city in Sardinia, was home to pirates—and is an archaeology lover’s dream | National Geographic Travelers visiting Sardinia should consider visiting Nora, an ancient Italian city turned archeological site with history yet to be uncovered. Dirk Renckhoff, Alamy Stock Photo TRAVEL This ancient city in Sardinia was home to pirates—and is an archaeology lover’s dream Nora doesn’t have the name recognition—or crowds—of Pompeii. But the well-preserved coastal settlement offers travelers a rare glimpse into the lives of the pirates, Vandals, Romans, Phoenicians, and Carthaginians who once laid claim to it. By Hannah Singleton Published February 10, 2026 Perched at the edge of a narrow peninsula in southern Sardinia , the ancient city of Nora is exposed to the elements. Wind, sun, salty air, and for centuries, even pirates. From every vantage point of the port city, residents and visitors can take in views of the Mediterranean Sea, which made Nora a thriving trade hub during the 8th century B.C. Nora doesn’t have the name recognition, impressive towering structures, or crowds of tourists like Pompeii or Ephesus. The ancient city, now a significant archaeological site, offers history buffs a rare glimpse of over 1,500 years of life in the ancient Sardinian city—a 43-minute drive from Cagliari. ( Seven historic islands in Europe you shouldn't miss .) The complex history of Nora The theater, marketplace, bath complex, old roads, and a temple—most of what’s above ground at Nora—date to the Roman period from 238 B.C. to the 5th century A.D. Paula Pugh, 61, from Swaffham, Norfolk, travelled from Stansted Airport to Calabria in southern Italy for a five-day holiday to celebrate her husband's birthday in September. After arriving she was told she had exceeded her 90-day visa-free allowance to the Schengen area and was put on a return flight, but Pugh said this was a database error and that she had only spent 22 days in the area. The European Commission said it is the responsibility of individual countries to correct any errors. The 61-year-old said the experience made her feel "like a criminal", but so far she has been unable to identify the source of the error. Her experience also cost her hundreds of pounds after she had to pay for her return flight back to the UK and she lost money she had already spent on the holiday. Pugh and her husband arrived at Reggio Calabria Airport at 12:40 BST but was denied entry. Desde la creación de la OIT, en 1919, sus normas internacionales del trabajo han pretendido establecer las aspiraciones, los valores y los derechos que se expresaron finalmente en la Carta de las Naciones Unidas (1945) y se proclamaron en la Declaración Universal de Derechos Humanos (1948): La fe en los derechos humanos fundamentales, en la dignidad y el valor de la persona humana y en la igualdad de derechos de hombres y mujeres, y la determinación de promover el progreso social y la mejora del nivel de vida con mayor libertad . En la actualidad, las normas internacionales del trabajo dan expresión a los derechos humanos en la esfera civil y política, así como en la esfera económica, social y cultural. La OIT colabora estrechamente con el sistema de las Naciones Unidas, a través de iniciativas tales como el Llamamiento a la Acción en Favor de los Derechos Humanos , a fin de promover las normas internacionales del trabajo como parte de las normas y estándares derechos humanos que son la base de la Agenda 2030 . Le norme internazionali del lavoro sono supportate da organi di controllo unici a livello internazionale, che contribuiscono a garantire l’applicazione delle convenzioni da parte dei paesi che le hanno ratificate. Analysis of the 18th-century musket balls indicates they were fired by colonial militia members at British forces during the North Bridge fight. The Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library is set to open in July 2026 outside Medora, North Dakota. Photograph by Image Professionals GmbH, Alamy Stock Photo By Stephanie Pearson Published October 21, 2025 Theodore Roosevelt first traveled to the Badlands on a hunting trip in 1883. He was so taken by the otherworldly landscape of pastel buttes, trilling meadowlarks, and disappearing bison, that he returned in 1884 to grieve the simultaneous deaths of his wife and mother, raising cattle and working on the wild frontier for almost three years. Its “desolate, grim beauty” so changed Roosevelt that he famously wrote, “I would not have been president had it not been for my experience in North Dakota .” Opening on July 4, 2026, the Theodore Roosevelt Presidential Library celebrates the Badlands as much as it does the 26th president. Designed by Norwegian architectural firm Snøhetta, the state-of-the-art, sustainable library sits high on a lonely butte outside of Medora, a military camp turned frontier town named after a French nobleman’s wife. The 93,000-square-foot library disappears into its surroundings, camouflaged by a living roof sprouting native plants, part of a 1.3-mile walking trail that provides sweeping views toward the national park. The Redding-based district office oversees field offices in Alturas, Arcata, Redding and Susanville and a field station in Cedarville. The district contains two distinct regions. On the east, the Applegate and Eagle Lake field offices oversee vast expanses of public lands in a high desert landscape, including about a million and a half acres in far western Nevada. Small communities depend on public lands for economic benefits, primarily through livestock grazing, and tourism uses ranging from hunting to mountain biking. These lands provide habitat for 14 wild horse herds and special status species, such as greater sage grouse. On the west, the Arcata and Redding field offices manage smaller, scattered blocks of public land with more emphasis on recreation demands from urban areas. pages.description: After scoring his first international goal in the 1-0 win over Ukraine, Northern Ireland boss Michael O'Neill says Terry Devlin is "a bit of a dream" to manage.
pages.text: Northern Ireland 1-0 Ukraine: The 'manager's dream' who has put NI one game from history - BBC Sport Image source, Press Eye Image caption, Terry Devlin scored his first Northern Ireland goal against Ukraine By Andy Gray BBC Sport NI Journalist Published 14 November 2026 It was a moment that Northern Ireland needed. When Terry Devlin picked the ball up on the edge of the area in the 68th minute against Ukraine there was only one thought in his mind. And when the ball flew into the corner Windsor Park erupted at another highlight of a Nations League campaign that has been a real feel-good story so far. Heading into Saturday's game they had yet to concede a goal, but the one thing they had lacked was a home win - or even a home goal - after drawing blanks in stalemates with Hungary and Georgia in Belfast. They had already come close when Jamie Donley slotted home in the first half but the forward had strayed offside, leaving the moment the hosts had been waiting for to come through Devlin's superb winner. It leaves Northern Ireland's Nations League fate in their own hands, and a draw or better in Hungary would secure promotion to League A for the first time. For Northern Ireland boss Michael O'Neill, it was a huge moment from a player who he said is "a bit of a dream" to manage. "Terry's a great lad. He deserves everything he'll get from the game and he's one of those lads that maximises what he has," O'Neill said about the 23-year-old Portsmouth defender. Better calibrations of the machines potentially can increase the accuracy of their diagnostic images by several times, according to NIST scientists. Notes from the Field: Measles Outbreak --- Indiana, June--July 2011 On June 20, 2011, an emergency department (ED) physician reported five epidemiologically linked measles cases to the Indiana State Department of Health. The subsequent investigation identified a total of 14 confirmed cases in northeast Indiana. Of these, 10 were laboratory-confirmed, and four were among household contacts of persons with laboratory-confirmed measles. Of the 14 patients, 13 were unvaccinated persons in the same extended family. The nonfamily member was a child aged 23 months who had received 1 dose of measles, mumps, and rubella vaccine 4 months before illness onset. Four of the 14 patients were males; median age was 11.5 years (range: 15 months--27 years). One patient was a woman in week 32 of pregnancy who was hospitalized for acute pneumonitis. Investigators learned that a third unvaccinated member of the household had developed fever and rash 11 days earlier, after returning to the United States from a 3-month visit to India, but measles had not been suspected until household contacts sought evaluation for similar symptoms. pages.text: Notre communauté - Internet Society Notre communauté Notre communauté Notre vaste et diverse communauté de plus de 150 000 bénévoles et 80 organisations apporte de véritables changements dans le monde entier. Ce réseau extraordinaire agit aux niveaux local, régional et mondial pour promouvoir notre vision d’un Internet ouvert, connecté à l’échelle mondiale, sécurisé et digne de confiance pour tout le monde. Qui compose notre communauté ? Membres individuels Nos membres individuels jouent un rôle essentiel dans la mise en œuvre de notre vision en contribuant à des projets menés par la communauté. Ils participent à des événements, des campagnes de plaidoyer et des initiatives d’autonomisation. Chapitres Nos chapitres accomplissent un travail remarquable (sur six continents !) pour répondre aux besoins de leurs communautés. Ils informent, sensibilisent et éduquent sur les enjeux liés à Internet, renforcent les capacités locales et favorisent la collaboration au sein des communautés. Groupes d’intérêts spéciaux (SIG) et groupes permanents (SG) Nos SIG et SG rassemblent des membres de l’Internet Society partageant les mêmes centres d’intérêt afin de travailler sur les enjeux liés à Internet qui leur tiennent le plus à cœur. Toute personne membre individuelle ou membre d’un chapitre peut rejoindre un SIG ou un SG. pages.text: Notre travail - Internet Society Notre travail Notre travail Œuvrer pour un Internet fiable et communautaire, accessible à tout le monde. Internet est une force transformatrice. Mais tout le monde n’en bénéficie pas de la même manière. Environ 2 milliards de personnes n’ont toujours pas accès à Internet. Et, de plus en plus, notre sécurité en ligne est mise en péril par le manque de confiance quant au contrôle de nos informations personnelles. Les enjeux n’ont jamais été aussi importants. C’est pourquoi nous nous associons aux communautés pour aider chacun à surmonter ses obstacles spécifiques à la connectivité, qu’ils soient géographiques, techniques, réglementaires ou financiers. Dans le cadre de notre Stratégie 2030, nous nous concentrons sur deux défis mondiaux majeurs auxquels Internet est confronté : Manque de confiance envers Internet . Parce que tout le monde mérite une expérience Internet sûre, sécurisée et respectueuse de sa vie privée. Inégalités mondiales . Parce que les personnes du monde entier doivent avoir accès à un Internet abordable, fiable et résilient. Découvrez nos activités pour l’année à venir dans notre Plan d’action 2026 . Guatemala) VUE D'ENSEMBLE DE L'AFFAIRE Dans cette affaire, le Liechtenstein demandait au Gouvernement du Guatemala redressement et réparation pour des mesures contraires au droit international que ce gouvernement aurait prises contre M. Friedrich Nottebohm, ressortissant du Liechtenstein. Le Guatemala a soulevé une exception d’incompétence, mais la Cour l’a rejetée dans son arrêt du 18 novembre 1953. Dans un deuxième arrêt, en date du 6 avril 1955, la Cour a déclaré irrecevable la demande du Liechtenstein pour des motifs ayant trait à la nationalité de M. Nottebohm. Seul le lien de nationalité entre un Etat et un individu donne à l’Etat le droit d’intenter une action internationale au nom de cet individu. M. Nottebohm, à l’époque ressortissant allemand, s’était établi au Guatemala en 1905 et avait continué à y résider. En octobre 1939, c’est-à-dire après le déclenchement de la seconde guerre mondiale, pendant un voyage en Europe, il avait obtenu la nationalité du Liechtenstein. En 1940, il était retourné au Guatemala et y avait repris la direction de ses affaires jusqu’en 1943, date de son éloignement par mesure de guerre. Sur le plan international, l’octroi de la nationalité ne peut entraîner la reconnaissance par d’autres Etats que s’il coïncide avec l’existence de liens authentiques entre l’individu et l’Etat qui lui accorde sa nationalité. River Action UK has accused Natural Resources Wales (NRW) of not doing enough to assess or address any risk to local rivers and and other water bodies when plans for three farms in Powys were approved last year. It follows years of debate over the alleged impact of chicken farming on rivers such as the Wye and Severn - in an area dubbed the UK's "poultry capital" . NRW said it would be inappropriate to comment ahead of the court case, but that it would "participate fully in the legal process". The case is about plans to increase the capacity of three Powys farms by a combined 336,900 chickens, bringing the total to 522,000. The three farms are Neuadd Isaf, Rhosddu and Llanshay. Two of the farms, Rhosddu and Llanshay, are in the River Severn catchment while Neuadd Isaf is in the River Wye catchment. Campaigners said the Severn was showing "signs of strain" with regular algal blooms, brown algae smothering the river

K., 20 October 2026 – The PyTorch Foundation, the vendor-neutral home for the open source intelligence layer, is announcing today that Nscale has joined as a Platinum member. Nscale is a full-stack AI cloud platform, bringing together power, data centers, compute and software in one vertically integrated platform. Nscale first came to the PyTorch Foundation’s project ecosystem through Ray, the open-source framework for distributed computing and scaling AI workloads. Following Nscale’s planned acquisition of Anyscale, the company behind Ray, Nscale has committed to continuing investment in Ray’s development and its contributor community, building on Ray’s governance under the Foundation since the project joined in October 2025. “ Most infrastructure providers treat the framework and the data center as two separate problems. We treat them as one. PyTorch has remained the base layer of AI because it kept the Pythonic style researchers know, while getting serious about performance. Ray, also part of the PyTorch Foundation, does something different: getting that work to run across thousands of GPUs. With Anyscale, the creators of Ray, set to join Nscale, we’re not just using that ecosystem, we’re building the infrastructure underneath it. pages.text: NSF 101: 5 tips on how to work with an NSF program officer | NSF - U.S. National Science Foundation Image file: View image credit NSF 101: 5 tips on how to work with an NSF program officer By Vincent Tedjasaputra, PhD February 23, 2021 Are you an undergraduate student thinking about how to get funding for graduate school? An early-career researcher looking to launch your new lab? An established researcher with dozens of years of funding from NSF under your belt? Whatever the phase of your research career, it is a good idea to reach out to an NSF program officer as the first step in the application process. Program officers are the heart and soul of NSF. They themselves are researchers - experts from the research community who guide grant proposals through Merit Review, part of the process that determines if a proposal is funded. Program officers are a valuable resource for both applicants and researchers who have been funded, as they can provide insight and often give direct feedback. Don't be intimidated to reach out to a program officer—they are there to help. The myth that reaching out might hinder your chances couldn't be further from the truth! In fact, you may be surprised at how helpful your program officer can be. Here are five tips from NSF program officers to help you work with them: 1. Do your homework If this is your first time interacting with NSF and you don't know or have a program officer for an active award, you can search the NSF funding website .
